California some grasses start their growth in late autumn and come into bloom in December, although others wait until spring.
Grassland owes its characteristics to the perennial grasses that constitute the dominant climax vegetation. These climax grasses may be tall or short and grow in bunches or as sod. Forbs occur mixed with the grasses, and variation in the time of blooming of these broad-leaved and mostly perennial herbs as well as of the grasses gives the grassland a variety of aspects like the forest. The prairie has beauty, character, and a history all its own.
Tall grass prairie is a highly productive agricultural land for corn, wheat, soybeans, and cereal crops in general. This is evident both in North America and Europe. Hogs and cattle are fattened on the corn that is grown. The more arid short grasslands are more hazardous to cultivate, as crops, mostly wheat, often fail during the dry years of climatic cycles. Plowed or overgrazed ground, destitute of grass or crop cover, is whipped up by strong winds to produce the great dust storms. Man has not always used the grasslands intelligently. He has plowed up land where the grass cover should have been left intact. Arid grazing lands are often over used by cattle. Ultimately pressed by economic incentives to produce more food, man has dug ditches to drain the wetlands in the prairies. Very little of the virgin plant associations have been left ungrazed or unplowed.
